featured.name: pi-hashline-edit-pro
featured.headline: Edits addressed by anchors, not line numbers
summary: Line numbers shift whenever something above them changes, and fuzzy matching can silently pick the wrong occurrence. pi-hashline-edit-pro avoids both by giving every served line a unique four-letter anchor. The anchor is the only address an edit may use, so inserting or deleting lines never invalidates the lines you did not touch.

It disables the built-in edit tool and registers read, replace, insert, anchor_grep, and undo_last_change instead. On its own 34-scenario benchmark it places first at 95.2% overall and 94.3% on the stale-and-drift cases, and the traces for every run are in the repository.

points.title: Anchors survive edits
points.body: Every served line carries its own anchor. An insertion or deletion reassigns nothing else, so a follow-up edit needs no re-read.

points.title: Stale edits are refused
points.body: The session remembers the text it served. If the file changed underneath, the tool returns [E_RANGE_STALE] and the current range instead of editing a neighbour.

points.title: Undo restores the bytes
points.body: The last replace or insert on a file reverts byte-for-byte, including BOM and line endings, and the undo record survives a session restart.

points.title: Batches are atomic
points.body: Edits to the same file are grouped into one batch with one diff and one undo. If any member is stale, the whole batch is refused and nothing is written.

projects.name: pi-unsloth-webtools
projects.tagline: Search, fetch, and render tools for pi with no API key: a seven-engine search with dedup and ranking, HTML-to-Markdown and PDF extraction ported from the Unsloth Studio codebase, and a Jina Reader fallback for pages that need JavaScript.

projects.name: pi-tor-proxy
projects.tagline: Routes every request the pi agent makes through Tor. It downloads and verifies its own Tor binary, gives each pi instance its own circuit, and checks the exit IP against check.torproject.org.
highlights: Downloads and SHA-256 verifies its own Tor binary

projects.name: pi-msg-workflow
projects.tagline: Numbered message and command stores plus configurable review workflows: a start phase, rounds that reset the context between passes, and a final commit or summary.
highlights: Rounds reset the context between passes

projects.name: pi-git-commit
projects.tagline: A commit flow that keeps an agent from committing carelessly: a bash guard for mutative git commands, a structured git_commit tool, and a /commit command that a human has to run first.
highlights: Mutative git commands in bash are blocked
FIX, IMPROVE, and NEW typed commits

projects.name: pi-edit-benchmark
projects.tagline: Drives real models through each editing tool's own tools and scores correctness, safety, and robustness, with a full trace for every run.
highlights: Stale and drift scenarios are scored
Every verdict links to its trace

principles: Make the wrong operation impossible, not merely discouraged.
Show the model exactly what it sees.
Put a human gate in front of anything destructive.
Measure before claiming, and publish the traces.
Keep the site static; let a scheduled job refresh the numbers.
about: I build extensions for pi, the terminal coding agent, and publish them on npm. The same pattern shows up in most of the work: an agent makes a change that looks right and is subtly wrong, and the fix is to make that failure impossible rather than paper over it.

pi-hashline-edit-pro is the main one. It replaces line numbers and fuzzy matching with four-letter anchors, refuses stale edits, and can undo byte-for-byte. When I wanted to know whether it was actually better than the alternatives, I wrote pi-edit-benchmark, ran 8 models over 34 scenarios, and published the traces, including the runs it loses.

The rest is here too: Tor routing, numbered review workflows, a guarded commit flow, and the web tools. The numbers on this page refresh from the GitHub and npm APIs every day through a scheduled workflow.

lab.intro: The figures come from committed run reports in pi-edit-benchmark, and every verdict links back to a trace. The rest of the numbers on this page refresh daily at 06:00 UTC.
